stages.name: Student Idea
stages.blurb: A student or faculty member has an idea and surfaces it somehow - usually through a WhatsApp group or a department coordinator. No portal exists at this stage.

stages.name: Innovation Cell / Council
stages.blurb: The IIC council meets quarterly and approves activities. The council-meeting upload is a hard gate: no meeting uploaded, no activities can be filed for that quarter.

stages.name: Evaluation
stages.blurb: YUKTI-NIR runs an institute-side verifier workflow with a Recommended / Not Recommended status. This is the only documented evaluation gate in the mandated stack.

stages.name: Incubation
stages.blurb: The institution registers an incubation unit on the IIC portal. No registered source describes the incubation workflow beyond unit registration.

stages.name: Mentor
stages.blurb: MAARG is the national mentorship platform. Internal mentor session records are undocumented across every registered source.

stages.name: Prototype
stages.blurb: YUKTI-NIR buckets innovations by TRL. Recommended entries auto-pool into ARIIA Section 4 - the single documentary join between the venture track and the data track.

stages.name: IPR
stages.blurb: The mandated portal has an IPR/TTO Centres menu that records a TTO's existence and floor area but has no field to record a patent. Patent tables live in annual reports and private registers.

stages.name: Market Validation
stages.blurb: No registered source describes institutional market-validation practice. All six questions are UNKNOWN by design.

stages.name: Funding
stages.blurb: DPIIT-recognised startups feed the NIRF FSI sub-metric. Per-startup rows are hand-typed per discipline per year with no auto-population from MCA, GST, ROC or DPIIT.

stages.name: Growth
stages.blurb: No registered source describes institutional growth-tracking practice. All six questions are UNKNOWN by design.

stages.name: Reporting
stages.blurb: Four mandated systems - IIC, YUKTI-NIR, ARIIA, NIRF - each with its own schema and (for IIC vs YUKTI) its own credentials. The annual report is hand-assembled from spreadsheets.

cells.question: what_happens
cells.answer: Students and faculty form ideas and surface them informally. Two NIT-level IICs differ ~75x in ideas generated under the same national programme, so the count is a function of local practice, not of any standard intake process.
cells.basis: P1-001 measures the 75x variance directly from published IIC reports. No source documents a standardised intake process.

cells.question: who_manages
cells.answer: Innovation Activity Coordinator (A-06) and IIC Members (A-12) collect; the Convener (A-03) controls what is presented to council. No source binds a named role specifically to idea intake.
cells.basis: The roles are documentary (Phase 2) and the Convener's agenda control is documentary, but the binding of any role to THIS stage is inferred from role descriptions, not stated.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: ask who actually receives an idea first, and whether that person is named in any institutional document.

cells.question: what_tool
cells.answer: No mandated portal for idea capture. IISc routes student coordination through WhatsApp (COMP-024); Diagram 5 reconstructs the coordinator asking in the same group.
cells.basis: COMP-024 is a direct quote from IISc's own coordination page. Diagram 5 is a marked reconstruction from official forms.
cells.still_needs: Internal tooling at this stage is UNKNOWN across every registered source (P-A10).

cells.question: what_data
cells.answer: Idea description, team, department - captured informally. No registered source documents an idea-capture schema.
cells.basis: P-A10 states internal tooling and schemas are UNKNOWN at every stage. No registered source documents an idea-capture form.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: capture the actual fields an institution records when an idea is first logged.

cells.question: where_breaks
cells.answer: Idea counts are not funnel-linked to downstream outputs: reported prototypes can exceed reported ideas, proving the fields are not one funnel.
cells.basis: P1-008 is measured directly from published IIC reports.

cells.question: manual_work
cells.answer: UNKNOWN. Phase 10 problem analysis P-A10 states hours are not measured and calls this the highest-value unknown in that section.
cells.basis: P-A10:554 is explicit: 'Not measured. This is the highest-value unknown in Section A.'
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B interview instrument: hours per idea logged, per quarter.

cells.question: what_happens
cells.answer: The IIC council meets quarterly. Minimum 3 IIC Calendar activities plus 1 Celebration per quarter, i.e. a 16+ activity/year baseline. Activities cannot be filed until the quarter's council meeting is uploaded.
cells.basis: GOV-020 states the activity minimums; GOV-019 states the council-meeting gate verbatim from the IIC portal.

cells.question: who_manages
cells.answer: IIC President (A-01) chairs and can change council membership; Convener (A-03) controls the quarterly agenda; nine named coordinator roles (A-04 to A-12) implement.
cells.basis: The full council role set is documented on the IIC portal (GOV-018) and mapped in Phase 2 against 25 institutional roles.

cells.question: what_tool
cells.answer: IIC Portal (mandated). Menu exposes dashboard, IIC performance, activity status, council status, student/faculty participation, incubation unit registration and e-Repository.
cells.basis: GOV-018 enumerates the portal's dashboard fields directly.

cells.question: what_data
cells.answer: Per activity: 4 social media links, participant counts, expenditure, video URL, 2 photographs and 1 document upload.
cells.basis: GOV-021 lists the per-activity report requirements verbatim from the IIC portal.

cells.question: where_breaks
cells.answer: The council-meeting upload gates the entire activity pipeline for the quarter. If the meeting is not uploaded, no activities can be added - a single missing artefact blocks 16+ downstream filings.
cells.basis: GOV-019 states the gate directly. Diagram 5 P5 independently names it as a pain point.

cells.question: manual_work
cells.answer: 16+ mandated activities/year, each carrying 4 social links + 2 photos + 1 video + 1 document = 8 evidence artefacts, so ~128+ artefacts/year per institution. Structural count MEASURED-FROM-DOCS; hours UNKNOWN.
cells.basis: The 16 and the 8 are both registered portal requirements. The product (~128) is arithmetic on two documentary numbers. Hours are not stated in any registered source.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: hours per activity report, and hours to assemble the quarterly evidence pack.

cells.question: what_happens
cells.answer: YUKTI-NIR runs an institute-side verification workflow. Status flow is Pending -> Recommended / Not Recommended. A Recommended entry is eligible for YIC, which in 2025 was open to TRL 4+ registered innovations.
cells.basis: GOV-023 states the verifier workflow and the YIC eligibility threshold directly from the IIC portal.

cells.question: who_manages
cells.answer: YUKTI Coordinator (A-04) verifies submissions - a gatekeeping act, but over YUKTI entries only. HEIs manage expert verification through an 'Add Verifier' tab.
cells.basis: GOV-023 documents the Add Verifier tab and the status flow; Phase 2 documents the A-04 role.

cells.question: what_tool
cells.answer: YUKTI-NIR, reachable from the IIC portal but under SEPARATE credentials: 'IIC login credentials and the YUKTI login credentials are different.'
cells.basis: GOV-025 is a verbatim portal statement about credential divergence.

cells.question: what_data
cells.answer: TRL bucket (Idea/PoC 1-4, Innovation/Prototype 5-9, Business/Startup), indexed on Themes & Stages, TRL, MRL and IRL.
cells.basis: GOV-023 enumerates the three TRL buckets and the four indexing axes.

cells.question: where_breaks
cells.answer: Two breaks. Separate credentials force a second login and a second identity. And IIC's own 'Rating and Scoring System' help page returns 'Coming Soon', so the star-rating formula is not publicly documented.
cells.basis: GOV-025 and GOV-044 are both verbatim portal observations.

cells.question: manual_work
cells.answer: Each recommended entry must be re-submitted downstream to ARIIA (auto-pool) and separately to NIRF (manual). The re-key is structural; the hours are UNKNOWN.
cells.basis: GOV-024 documents the ARIIA auto-pool; GOV-028 documents that NIRF does not auto-populate. The inference is that the coordinator therefore re-keys at least once.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: hours per YUKTI entry, and whether the coordinator re-keys or copies.

cells.question: what_happens
cells.answer: The institution registers an incubation unit on the IIC portal. No registered source describes the incubation workflow beyond unit registration.
cells.basis: GOV-018 lists 'incubation unit registration' as a dashboard field. No source documents workflow beyond it.

cells.question: who_manages
cells.answer: Incubation Manager / TBI Manager (B-03) is the named role. Phase 2 found no procurement role for it in any source it read.
cells.basis: P2-001 is the IIC portal's own guidance on who should be Convener; P2-011 is the named office-holder list. Phase 2 records B-03's procurement role as 'No procurement role found in any source read' and its spend authority as UNKNOWN. The documented absence is the finding.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: does the Incubation Manager hold a budget line, and at what ceiling?

cells.question: what_tool
cells.answer: IIC Portal has an incubation unit registration field. Internal incubation tooling is UNKNOWN across every registered source.
cells.basis: GOV-018 documents the registration field. COMP-026 quotes two ERP vendors describing departments keeping their own registers.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: what system holds the incubation cohort, and is it a spreadsheet?

cells.question: what_data
cells.answer: Unit existence and (for TTOs) floor area. No venture-level incubation record schema is documented in any registered source.
cells.basis: GOV-018 documents unit registration; GOV-022 documents the IPR/TTO menu's limited field set (existence + floor area).
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: what per-venture fields the institution actually maintains inside the incubation unit.

cells.question: where_breaks
cells.answer: Departments outside the system keep their own registers. DigiERP's own marketing states the institution 'carries both the software cost and the duplicate work'.
cells.basis: COMP-026 is a verbatim vendor statement about departmental duplicate registers.

cells.question: manual_work
cells.answer: UNKNOWN.
cells.basis: P-A10 records internal incubation tooling and hours as UNKNOWN.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: hours per incubation unit per year, and how many ventures are tracked inside it.

cells.question: what_happens
cells.answer: MAARG is the national mentorship platform, with AI matchmaking, session scheduling, cohort programmes and dashboards.
cells.basis: GOV-041 enumerates MAARG's four capabilities directly from Startup India.

cells.question: who_manages
cells.answer: IIC Member (A-12) and Entrepreneurship Cell (B-04). Mentorship coordination is problem area 5.
cells.basis: The roles are documentary; the binding of either to mentorship is inferred from role titles, not stated.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: who owns the mentor roster, and does that person appear in any institutional document?
cells.cross_ref: Phase 2 roles A-12, B-04; problem area 5

cells.question: what_tool
cells.answer: MAARG (mandated, GOV-041). Internal mentor-session records are UNKNOWN; Diagram 5 reconstructs mentorship in WhatsApp threads.
cells.basis: GOV-041 documents MAARG. Diagram 5 N10 is a marked reconstruction from official forms.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: does the institution log mentor sessions anywhere, and where?

cells.question: what_data
cells.answer: Mentor profiles, matching, session logs. Schema undocumented in every registered source.
cells.basis: No registered source documents an internal mentor-session schema.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: capture the mentor-session record fields, if any.

cells.question: where_breaks
cells.answer: No permissions model - mentors see everything. Diagram 5 names this as pain point P3.
cells.basis: Diagram 5 P3 is a marked reconstruction. It is the only source naming the permissions gap; no registered documentary source states it.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: confirm whether mentor visibility is actually unrestricted, and whether NDA-tiered access is ever discussed internally.

cells.question: manual_work
cells.answer: UNKNOWN.
cells.basis: No registered source measures mentorship hours.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: hours per mentor per month, and hours to arrange a session.

cells.question: what_happens
cells.answer: YUKTI-NIR buckets innovations by TRL: Idea/PoC (1-4), Innovation/Prototype (5-9), Business/Startup. Recommended entries auto-pool into ARIIA Section 4.
cells.basis: GOV-023 gives the TRL buckets; GOV-024 states the ARIIA auto-pool.

cells.question: who_manages
cells.answer: YUKTI Coordinator (A-04) verifies; HEI manages verifiers through the 'Add Verifier' tab. Status: Pending -> Recommended / Not Recommended.
cells.basis: GOV-023 documents the Add Verifier tab and status flow.

cells.question: what_tool
cells.answer: YUKTI-NIR, separate login. No venture lifecycle, no funding ledger, no IP docket, no cohort management - YUKTI is a submission plus verification queue with three static buckets.
cells.basis: GOV-025 documents the credential split. The absence of lifecycle features is documented in the Phase 4 ecosystem deep-dive (GOV-023 scope).

cells.question: what_data
cells.answer: TRL, MRL and IRL indexing; Theme & Stage tags; a Recommended status that becomes the ARIIA Section 4 record.
cells.basis: GOV-023 and GOV-024 both document the indexing and the auto-pool.

cells.question: where_breaks
cells.answer: The auto-pool is one-directional and scoped to ARIIA only. NIRF Innovation screens show no evidence of auto-population from YUKTI, so a Recommended prototype still has to be re-keyed for NIRF.
cells.basis: GOV-024 states the ARIIA auto-pool; GOV-028 documents NIRF's own per-discipline capture with no auto-population. The absence of a YUKTI->NIRF write path is the core two-track finding.

cells.question: manual_work
cells.answer: One YUKTI entry does NOT equal one NIRF row: NIRF requires ~11 screens per discipline, so a 4-discipline university files the Innovation form 4x. Structural count MEASURED-FROM-DOCS; hours UNKNOWN.
cells.basis: GOV-028 documents the per-discipline repetition. The 4x is arithmetic on that documentary number.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: hours per YUKTI entry, and hours per NIRF discipline row.

cells.question: what_happens
cells.answer: IIC has an 'IPR/TTO Centres' menu that registers a TTO's existence and floor area but has NO field to record a patent. Institutions file patent tables separately, usually in the annual report, often splitting granted / published / filed.
cells.basis: GOV-022 states the menu's field set directly. P1-009 measures the granted/published/filed split from published reports.

cells.question: who_manages
cells.answer: IPR Activity Coordinator (A-08) brings IPR matters to council. A named IPR/TTO Cell with a named in-charge is achievable but rare.
cells.basis: P1-006 measures the rarity of a named IPR/TTO Cell directly from published reports.

cells.question: what_tool
cells.answer: No mandated patent register. ARIIA DCS requires 'Patent Application No', 'Year of Patent Application', 'Current Status' and 'IP / Patented Technology' per innovation - fields the IIC portal does not carry.
cells.basis: COMP-032 enumerates ARIIA's per-patent DCS fields; GOV-022 documents the IIC portal's absence of a patent field.

cells.question: what_data
cells.answer: Granted / published / filed split (P1-009). A Yes/No commercialisation column already exists in some institutional IP registers (P1-016). Foreign IP has no field anywhere (P1-012).
cells.basis: All three are measured directly from published IIC reports and IP registers.

cells.question: where_breaks
cells.answer: The mandated portal cannot record a patent, and foreign IP has no field. Separately, NIDHI-PRAYAS 2.0 requires an NOC confirming IP vests entirely with the innovator or startup - a requirement with no portal to enforce it.
cells.basis: GOV-022, P1-012 and GOV-037 are each documented: the portal gap, the foreign-IP gap, and the NIDHI-PRAYAS NOC requirement.

cells.question: manual_work
cells.answer: Four-year IP tables are common but frequently unreadable by text extraction (P1-010). Diagram 5 reconstructs patents tracked in a private register, re-keyed every year.
cells.basis: P1-010 measures the unreadability problem directly. Diagram 5 N9 is a marked reconstruction.

cells.question: what_happens
cells.answer: DPIIT-recognised startups feed the NIRF FSI sub-metric SU = 20 x f(N_vsp), where N_vsp = DPIIT-recognised startups in the previous three years. NIDHI-PRAYAS 2.0 requires an NOC confirming IP vests entirely with the innovator or startup.
cells.basis: GOV-027 states the SU formula; GOV-037 states the NIDHI-PRAYAS NOC requirement.

cells.question: who_manages
cells.answer: Startup Activity Coordinator (A-09) implements. Institutional spend authority sits with VC/Director (B-01) and Dean (B-02) at documented ceilings. Four Phase 2 roles carry documented spend authority: B-01, B-02, C-01 (Registrar) and C-03 (Finance Officer).
cells.basis: P2-003 (NIT Warangal: Director all cases; Registrar / Dean (R&D) Rs 10,00,000 non-consumable), P2-004 (HoD at Rs 1L, Dean (P&D) at Rs 3L), P2-006 (CRSU: Central Purchase Committee headed by VC above Rs 2 lakhs) and P2-011 (Startup Activity Coordinator = Faculty-in-Charge Incubation Centre) together establish the chain. CORRECTION: the Phase 2 B-01 free-text field says 'one of only two roles', but Phase 2's own grade field records four roles with documented spend authority (B-01, B-02, C-01, C-03). The grade field is used here; the stale prose in data_p2_roles.py line 354 is not.
cells.cross_ref: Phase 2 roles A-09, B-01, B-02, C-01, C-03

cells.question: what_tool
cells.answer: NIRF Innovation DCS per-startup rows. No funding ledger is mandated by any registered portal.
cells.basis: GOV-028 enumerates the NIRF per-startup capture fields. No registered source documents a mandated funding ledger.

cells.question: what_data

cells.basis: GOV-028 lists all seven per-startup fields verbatim from the NIRF DCS.

cells.answer: The awareness-spend field can carry a budget proposal rather than an actual, and the gap to real grants is 40x. Money fields carry sponsor identity and purpose, not just a number.
cells.basis: P1-023 measures the 40x proposal-vs-actual gap; P1-013 measures the sponsor-identity contamination. Both are measured from published IIC reports.

cells.question: what_happens
cells.answer: Institutions hand-assemble annual reports from spreadsheets and file IIC, YUKTI-NIR, ARIIA and NIRF returns. A single IIC report can carry two irreconcilable values for the same KPI field.
cells.basis: P1-002 measures the within-document contradiction directly from published IIC reports. P-A10 documents the hand-consolidation from departmental silos.

cells.question: who_manages
cells.answer: ARIIA Coordinator (A-10) and NIRF Coordinator (A-11) advise council on rank improvement. ARIIA's own DCS fetches from IIC, NISP, YUKTI and Innovation Ambassador portals.
cells.basis: GOV-031 states the ARIIA DCS fetch behaviour verbatim. Phase 2 documents both coordinator roles.

cells.question: what_tool
cells.answer: Four mandated systems: IIC Portal, YUKTI-NIR, ARIIA DCS and NIRF DCS. IIC and YUKTI use separate credentials. No public API, developer documentation or bulk export exists for any of them.
cells.basis: GOV-018 and GOV-025 document the portals and the credential split; GOV-043 states the absence of any public API or bulk export.

cells.question: what_data
cells.answer: ARIIA DCS fetches from IIC, NISP, YUKTI and Innovation Ambassador portals. NIRF Innovation is ~11 screens per discipline, so a 4-discipline university files the Innovation form 4x.
cells.basis: GOV-031 states the ARIIA fetch; GOV-028 documents the per-discipline repetition. The 4x is arithmetic on the documentary 11-screen figure.

cells.question: where_breaks
cells.answer: One IIC report can carry two irreconcilable values for the same KPI field (P1-002). Money fields carry sponsor identity and purpose, not just a number (P1-013). 'In-progress' is used as a value in a money field on a filed report (P1-025).
cells.basis: All three are measured directly from published IIC reports.

cells.question: manual_work
cells.answer: A university with 4 disciplines files the NIRF Innovation form 4x. None of the per-startup or per-patent data auto-populates. Structural count MEASURED-FROM-DOCS; hours UNKNOWN.
cells.basis: GOV-028 documents the repetition. P-A10:554 states hours are not measured.
cells.still_needs: Phase 3B: total hours per reporting cycle across all four systems.

two_track.join_evidence: YUKTI-NIR entries with 'Recommended' status auto-pool into ARIIA Section 4. This is the only documentary join between the two tracks, and it is one-directional: ARIIA pulls, with no shared write path back, scoped to ARIIA only, and it does not remove NIRF-I.
two_track.note: StartupHub's wedge is the join neither portal implements: a single venture record that emits all four submissions as a by-product, keyed on the entity and its state over time.

breakpoints.title: Council-meeting upload gates all activity filing
breakpoints.detail: If the quarterly council meeting is not uploaded, no activities can be added for that quarter - a single missing artefact blocks 16+ downstream filings.

breakpoints.title: 16+ activities/year x 8 evidence artefacts = 128+ artefacts
breakpoints.detail: Each activity report requires 4 social links, 2 photos, 1 video and 1 document. The volume is structural and mandatory.

breakpoints.title: Two tracks never join: YUKTI auto-pools to ARIIA but not to NIRF
breakpoints.detail: The ARIIA auto-pool is one-directional and ARIIA-scoped. NIRF screens show no evidence of auto-population from YUKTI, so every recommended prototype is re-keyed for NIRF.

breakpoints.title: IIC and YUKTI use different credentials
breakpoints.detail: The portal states IIC and YUKTI logins are different - a second identity for the same coordinator.

breakpoints.title: IIC star-rating formula is undocumented ('Coming Soon')
breakpoints.detail: The official Rating and Scoring help page returns 'Coming Soon'. A product that promises to optimise the star rating is promising against an unpublished formula.

breakpoints.title: The mandated portal has no field to record a patent
breakpoints.detail: IIC's IPR/TTO Centres menu registers TTO existence and floor area only. ARIIA DCS requires per-patent fields the IIC portal does not carry.

breakpoints.title: Budget proposals filed in actuals fields; gap to real grants 40x
breakpoints.detail: The awareness-spend field can carry a proposal rather than an actual. Money fields also carry sponsor identity and purpose instead of a number.

breakpoints.title: Same KPI field carries two irreconcilable values in one report
breakpoints.detail: Measured directly from published IIC reports. Relational integrity is absent at the schema level.

breakpoints.title: No public API or bulk export for any mandated portal
breakpoints.detail: No public API, developer documentation or bulk export found for IIC, YUKTI, NIRF, AISHE or MAARG. Every integration is therefore manual or screen-scraped.

breakpoints.title: NIRF Innovation filed per discipline, not per institution
breakpoints.detail: ~11 screens per discipline. A 4-discipline university files the same startup rows 4 times.

breakpoints.title: Departments outside the system keep their own registers
breakpoints.detail: ERP vendors' own marketing states the institution carries both the software cost and the duplicate work.

breakpoints.title: No permissions model - mentors see everything
breakpoints.detail: Diagram 5 names this as pain point P3. NDA-tiered visibility is absent.

breakpoints.title: Prototypes reported exceed ideas reported
breakpoints.detail: The idea and prototype fields are not one funnel. Reported prototypes can exceed reported ideas.

breakpoints.title: Text in money fields ('In-progress') on filed reports
breakpoints.detail: Measured from published IIC reports. Numeric validation is absent at the portal schema level.

manual_work.metric: Mandated activities per institution per year
manual_work.detail: 3 IIC Calendar activities per quarter (12/yr) plus 1 Celebration per quarter (4/yr).
4 social media links + 2 photographs + 1 video URL + 1 document upload.

manual_work.metric: Evidence artefacts per institution per year
manual_work.detail: 16+ activities x 8 artefacts. Arithmetic on two registered portal requirements.
A university with 4 disciplines files the Innovation form 4x.
Name, DPIIT number, amount, funding organisation, year, achievement level, investment type - per discipline per year, with no auto-population from MCA, GST, ROC or DPIIT.
IIC Portal, YUKTI-NIR, ARIIA DCS, NIRF Innovation - two of which (IIC, YUKTI) use separate credentials.

manual_work.metric: Institutional roles on the IIC council alone
manual_work.detail: President, VP, Convener and nine named coordinator roles, on top of the 25 institutional roles mapped in Phase 2.

manual_work.metric: Hours of manual consolidation per reporting cycle
manual_work.detail: Phase 10 P-A10 states this is not measured and calls it the highest-value unknown in Section A.

manual_work.metric: Rupees spent on manual reporting labour per year
manual_work.detail: No registered source prices the labour. OQ-03 (willingness to pay) is unmeasured and blocked on Phase 3B.
No registered source measures idea-intake effort.

external_benchmarks.name: NIRF Innovation parameters 2025
external_benchmarks.detail: FSI 0.25, IA 0.15, RIO 0.30, PII 0.10, AIE 0.10, Perception 0.10. Weights changed from 2024.
external_benchmarks.relevance: Sets the scoring surface StartupHub's reporting output must satisfy.

external_benchmarks.name: NIRF FSI startup sub-metric
external_benchmarks.detail: SU = 20 x f(N_vsp), N_vsp = DPIIT-recognised startups in previous 3 years. 5 marks of the final Innovation score hinge on one countable.
external_benchmarks.relevance: The single most quantified institutional incentive in the mandated stack.

external_benchmarks.name: ARIIA DCS cross-portal fetch
external_benchmarks.detail: ARIIA fetches from IIC, NISP, YUKTI and Innovation Ambassador portals, reducing submission effort by checking redundancy. One-directional, ARIIA-scoped only.
external_benchmarks.relevance: The only existing cross-portal de-duplication, and the template for what StartupHub generalises.

external_benchmarks.name: Factly/Dataful NIRF startup dataset
external_benchmarks.detail: 6,817 rows, 204 institutions, 5,490 distinct ventures, 4,538 registration numbers, 26 states, 80 cities, 2024-2026. Monetised from public DCS PDFs.
external_benchmarks.relevance: Proves institution-submitted innovation data is already public and already packaged by a third party.

external_benchmarks.name: State Startup Ranking (SRF) 5.0
external_benchmarks.detail: Results announced 16 Jan 2026; 34 States/UTs participated; 19 Action Points, 6 Reform Areas. Best Performer Cat A = Gujarat.
external_benchmarks.relevance: State-level pressure that propagates down to HEI reporting expectations.

external_benchmarks.name: Maharashtra Startup Policy 2025
external_benchmarks.detail: Commits to an online system mapping startups, incubators, accelerators, innovation labs, investors and mentors under a unique ID.
external_benchmarks.relevance: A state building the registry StartupHub would sit under - both a channel and a competitive risk.

external_benchmarks.name: NIDHI-PRAYAS 2.0 NOC requirement
external_benchmarks.detail: Students/faculty must submit an NOC confirming IP vests entirely with the innovator or startup.
external_benchmarks.relevance: An IP-vesting requirement with no portal to enforce it - StartupHub's IPR docket (D2) is the enforcement point.

external_benchmarks.name: MeitY Startup Hub IP due diligence
external_benchmarks.detail: Mandates TRL benchmarking and IP due diligence: ownership clarity, freedom to operate, defensibility. Distinguishes ownership vs a 2-year university tech-transfer licence.
external_benchmarks.relevance: The most explicit institutional statement that TRL and IP must be joined - StartupHub D1 + D2.

external_benchmarks.name: BHASKAR ID
external_benchmarks.detail: DPIIT launched BHASKAR (Bharat Startup Knowledge Access Registry) 16 Sep 2024, issuing an ecosystem-universal BHASKAR ID.
external_benchmarks.relevance: A national identity layer StartupHub must key to, not duplicate.

external_benchmarks.name: National Startup Master Data (planned)
external_benchmarks.detail: DPIIT plans to overhaul BHASKAR into a National Startup Master Data registry tracking the startup lifecycle. MeitY Startup Hub floated a similar tender.
external_benchmarks.relevance: The largest structural risk and the largest channel opportunity in the segment.

external_benchmarks.name: MAARG national mentorship platform
external_benchmarks.detail: AI matchmaking, session scheduling, cohort programmes and dashboards.
external_benchmarks.relevance: Mandated mentorship surface; StartupHub must integrate, not compete.

external_benchmarks.name: Kerala Startup Mission scale
external_benchmarks.detail: 375+ IEDCs across colleges and universities, 27 R&D institutions, 63 incubators; issues a KSUM UID as a third identity layer.
external_benchmarks.relevance: The densest documented state ecosystem and a model for how far a UID layer can reach.
